instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《弥阿之书》
类型：抄本
描述：记述了“沙漠漫游者的五次造访”——可能是被称为浪游旅人的那位司辰对弥阿城的造访。她最开始是个快乐的孩子——可能甚至只是个凡人——但之后事态愈发糟糕……
 “第二次造访时，她化为笑鸫。她的内心轻松愉悦，她的喙中饱含欢歌。但在她的羽毛碰触到城市的岩石的那一刻，那笑声便开始……”
 在倒数第二次造访时，漫游者化为蜈蚣，她的毒液“让岩石开裂”。弥阿被弃于沙漠。而她最后一次归来时，再次化为笑鸫，与同样变成鸟形的另外四位司辰一起，“在她可憎亲族的白骨上庆贺第一栖木的建立。”
output:
Name: Book of Miah
Type: codex
Description: An account of the 'five visits of the Desert Wanderer' - probably the Hour called the Vagabond - to the city Miah. She begins as a delighted child - perhaps even a mortal - but things then go badly…
 'In her second visit, she came as Laughingthrush. Her heart was bright within, her beak was ripe with song, but in the first moment her feathers touched the city stones, the laughter began….'
 The Wanderer's penultimate visit is as Centipede, whose 'venom cracks stone'. Miah is abandoned to the desert. But she returns one last time, again as Laughingthrush, with four other Hours who take the shape of birds, 'to celebrate the First Roost above the bones of her hated kin.'

 “有太多关于她遗产的故事，有太多关于她生还的传闻。我们更倾向于相信那对孪生孙女逃过一劫——甚至认定她们仍然生活在海洋彼端……”
 西奥神父开始相信，伊娃是为了摆脱家族的诅咒——她的祖先哈芙伦的“苍白遗产”，或者是亨德里克·德沃尔夫时期神汉红威廉对家族施加的诅咒。他在开篇认为这两个诅咒都子虚乌有；但在本书结尾，他决定宁可信其有，而不是把三人的死亡视作一场徒劳的悲剧。“摆脱对信仰的长期依赖并不那么容易，”他总结道。
output:
Name: Lady Eva's Repose
Type: codex
Description: A 'meditation' on the drowning of Lady Eva Dewulf and her two grandchildren, written in the years when the estate was abandoned by Father Theo, once the Dewulf family chaplain, one of the few to remain on the Isle in those desolate years.
 'There are so many stories of her heritage, so many rumours of her persistence. We might easily choose to believe that the grand-twins escaped - even that they live yet beyond the sea - '
 Father Theo has come to believe that Eva sought an escape from a family curse - the 'pale heritage' of Hafren her forebear, or the curse placed upon the line by the cunning-man Red William in the time of Hendrik Dewulf. He had begun by believing neither curse was real; but as the book concludes, he decides that he has determined to believe in them, rather than accept the three deaths as a futile tragedy. 'One does not so easily escape the long necessity of faith,' he concludes.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《大卫·格林爵士的日志·1903》
类型：抄本
描述：格林写的一本机密日志，他曾是夜勤处的警司，并于1903年就任居屋的图书管理员一职。格林用希克索斯语写了这本日志，大概是为了极端地保护他的隐私。
 1903年，居屋和夜勤处合作密切，而格林则是这场合作明面上的代言人。然而，显然格林私底下对夜勤处失望至极，他愈发认为其没有履行好职责。他对建造在布兰库格监狱下方的“镇压装置”尤为担忧。
“司辰和具名者都很危险，”他写道，“但至少我们应对祂们的措施都建立在长期的经验之上。但这样一位司辰：行动早于诞生之神——自从未进入之处离去之神——如果她的具名者行于世间，我们要如何才能了解祂们的能力与行动方式？”
 交替出现的算式（潮汐，日期，财务测算）和对“A·F”的热望的表述组成了日志最后的记录。格林似乎打算带着A·F远走高飞，其中有些算式表明，他一直以来都在挪用资金，奥尔图基奥事件及随后夜勤处重组为防剿局时的混乱局面为其提供了掩护……然而，这些记录在这年结束前便戛然而止。格林是否真的带着这些资金与挚友潜逃，以及他是否出于其他原因丢弃了这本日志，均不明了。
output:
Name: Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903
Type: codex
Description: A confidential journal kept by Greene, former Nocturnal Branch Superindent but, by 1903, Librarian of the House. Greene has kept his journal in Hyksos, presumably as an extra measure of privacy.
 In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'
 The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau... 

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input: Name: De Ratio Quercuum Type: codex Description: In English the title translates roughly as 'the Account of the Oaks'; but this is Nathaniel Darcy-Evers' fascinating, if haphazard, survey of the occult properties of every tree he can find, not just oaks. 'In Persia taxus baccata, the yew, is called sorkhdar, which is 'the red tree'. There they had long understood the Grail-Root. In later times, the Great King of Pontus had bee-hives set in the branches of the oldest of the female trees….' 'The berries of the Pontine Yew open the door to death but the honey of their flowers opens a different door entirely. This was not the Great King's mithridate but one who has suckled at the Great Yew fears poison no longer. Perhaps they should…' Nathaniel is here distracted, however, by the toxic properties of certain inks. He does mention more usefully that the minor Ink of Power, Yewgall, can be brewed through the Rites of the Roots with the assistance of the aspect Nectar.
output: 名称：De Ratio Quercuum 类型：抄本 描述：标题的拉丁语大意为“橡树之理”；但实际上是纳撒尼尔·达西-埃弗斯对他所能找到的所有树木其神秘学特性的调查，而非仅仅是橡树。本书虽杂乱无章，却引人入胜。 “在波斯，taxus baccata，即紫杉，被称为sorkhdar，意为‘红色的树’。他们对杯之根系早有了解。再后来，本都的伟大国王在最古老的雌树的枝条上安置了蜂箱……” “本都紫杉的浆果开启通往死亡的大门，但它的蜂蜜却能打开一扇截然不同的大门。这不是那位伟大国王的mithridate（万灵药），但饮下了伟大紫杉馈赠的人确实能够百毒不侵。也许他们应该……”但写到这里时，纳撒尼尔被某种墨水的毒性分散了注意力。他确实提到了更加有用的信息，那就是可以使用“根系之仪”，在蜜相的帮助下调制出一种次要的力量之墨，杉瘿墨。

 书中罕有对个人生活的细节描写。作为一名才华横溢的天文学家和窥天术家，托马斯客观而详尽地描述了自己的观测结果，以及在守夜人塔的塔顶建造天文台的过程。
 在记录到1577年的大彗星时，文章的风格才终于变得更活泼了些，但同时也更含糊不清。托马斯引用了恰巧与他同名的人物，拂晓时期的托马斯院长的观点——后者是研究“低层天界的风，月，与卵壳”的权威。他评论道：“我的前辈知道这个真理：守夜人之树有三朵花：纸，墨，与火。现在我确证，大彗星正是那火焰。”
output:

Type: codex
Description: Thomas Dewulf, 2nd Baron Brancrug, was nicknamed 'Baron Silence of Castle Silence' for his taciturn severity - most likely the origin, eventually, of the name 'Hush House'.
 There are very few personal details here. Thomas, a talented astronomer and ouranoscopist, dispassionately details his observations and the building of the observatory atop the Watchman's Tower.
 As he records the passing of the Great Comet in 1577, the tone finally becomes more animated but also more obscure. Thomas cites his Dawn Period namesake, Abbot Thomas, as an authority on 'Wind, Moon, and Shell in the Heavens Inferior'. He observes: 'My predecessor knew this Truth - three Blossoms hath the Watchman's Tree: Paper; Ink; and Flame. The Great Comet, I now aver, is that Flame.'

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持阴郁庄严、带有神秘主义与宗教神话色彩的文风。
input:
Name: Opus Magnum Caeruleum
Type: codex
Description: Ambrose Westcott used to render the title of this venerable and anonymous work mockingly as 'the Big Blue Business'. A kinder translation would be 'the Great Work in Azure'.
 The reasons for Westcott's enmity to this work are clear to any pyroglyphicist: it was written at least two centuries before he was born, but anticipates or undermines many of his preferred conclusions.
 The 'Work' in question is the creation of the 'blue gold' allegedly necessary for the terrible Rite which allows a Forge-long to become a Name. The book mentions that Pyroglyphics techniques can be used with Forge to create Iotic Essence as a necessary component; but withholds the final step, insisting that the consequences are too dire, and that any interest should remain only a matter of theory.
output: 名称：Opus Magnum Caeruleum 类型：抄本 描述：这本匿名著作的标题曾被安布罗斯·威斯考特戏谑地翻译为“蓝色大把戏”。而更公允的翻译应当是“蔚蓝大功业”。 威斯考特对这本著作抱有敌意的原因对任何焰篆学家来说都是显而易见的：本作至少在他出生两个世纪前就写成，却预见或动摇了许多他青睐的结论。 此述中的“功业”指的是“蓝金”的制作过程，依其叙述，在将铸之长生者擢升为具名者的可怕仪式中，这种材料是必需的。书中提到，将“焰篆体”之技术与铸一起使用，可以提炼出必要的中间产物，赤化精华；却拒绝透露最后的步骤，作者坚称这么做的后果太过可怕，因此对它的任何兴趣都只应停留在理论层面上。

The original is notoriously incoherent - much later, Christopher Illopoly took on the task of editing and glossing it. He has taken some liberties, but the updated version is generally well regarded. Description: An eccentric political tract by Valentine Dewulf.
 Valentine suggests that rulers should be elected to govern by serpents, not their subjects, 'for the Serpent, being cold-blooded in its Nature, is incorruptible.'
 Valentine's initial proposal is that a college of electors should subject themselves to the bites of venomous serpents - which he grades and details, preferring the least dangerous - and should allow the resulting deliria to guide them in their choice of people's representatives. He becomes concerned, however, by the practicalities of ensuring equal quantities of venom in each case, and gets half-way into a proposal for using birds instead in the selection process, before giving up mid-sentence.
output:
名称：《毒牙的共和》
类型：抄本

 瓦伦丁提议说，统治者应当由毒蛇来选举产生，而不是由他们的臣民，“因蛇天性冷血，不可腐蚀。”
 瓦伦丁最初的建议是，所有的选民都应该主动接受毒蛇的啃咬——他在书中对毒蛇进行了评级和详述，推荐了危险性最小的——并让中毒产生的谵妄指导他们选出人民的代表。然而，他开始担心在不同情况下确保使用等量毒液的可行性，作为折中提出了使用鸟类的替代方案——但这项讨论只进行到一半就被放弃了。

 班克罗夫特是个极有天赋的学徒，但他把自己的精力投在一些徒劳无益且异想天开的计划：为漫宿的灵体举办“摘葡萄大赛”，教擂击者玩杂耍，还有为玫瑰女巫艾尔郡变出想象中的鲜花风暴，后者甚至连与他交合都坚决拒绝。班克罗夫特花了二十页篇幅哀叹此事。
 本书记载的梵咒既高等又艰深，这种魔法可以让一个人将其灵魂献给守夜人，开启飞升至居屋之路。班克罗夫特一喝高就会夸耀自己能背诵这一梵咒。他还给它谱上曲，在沃克斯豪尔花园的烟火大会上表演。

 Bancroft seems to have been a talented adept, but devoted his energies to frustratingly whimsical projects: arranging 'grape-fetching races' between Mansus-spirits, teaching Percussigants to juggle, and conjuring storms of imaginary blossoms for the rose-witch Ayrshire, who resolutely refused ever to couple with him. Bancroft spends twenty pages bemoaning this last.
 The Mantra here recorded is a high and exacting magic which can be used to pledge one's spirit to the Watchman, beginning an ascent to the House. Bancroft boasts of his ability to recite it when in his cups. He also had it set to music for a performance with fireworks at Vauxhall Gardens.

 Lord Franklin Bancroft, sometimes called the Prince of Wines, begins a series of visits to Brancrug House. His relationship with Eva becomes a source of scandal. Eva is by now forty-nine, but rumours persist for years of a Dewulf-Bancroft heir. Eva's biographer claims that before her 'drowning death', her child by Bancroft was adopted by her friends the Southeys - that the child became the sister of the later Poet Laureate, Robert Southey. instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, preserving the solemn, ritualistic tone and occult atmosphere.
input: 名称：《五大创造论》 类型：抄本 描述：游学者肖黑在本书中讨论了五种人类可能的起源，并佐以一个蒙面的，自称为拾滩鸦的形象。肖黑之后又称这些描述已全部被证伪，但无论如何，讨论本身还是被记录了下来。 “介壳源：我们诞自甲壳，如同黄蜂的孩子从蜘蛛体内钻出。辉源：我们生命的微粒降自“光”。受污之源：我们出世时浑身赤裸，身上沾着林地根部的淤泥……” 肖黑偏爱的理论是：我们是直立行走的猿猴的子孙，尽管他说及此论时语带讥讽；又或者我们不仅摄食了我们的父母，“此行并非天孽”，也摄食了我们的起源，所以我们来自虚界。
output:
Name: Five Creations
Type: codex
Description: The itinerant scholar Shohei debated five possible origins for humanity with a hooded figure since claimed to be the Beach-Crow. Shohei later claimed that all these accounts had proven false, but the debate was, nevertheless, recorded.
 THE CARAPACE ORIGIN: we were born from shell, like the children of the wasp from the spider. THE GLORIOUS ORIGIN: our life-motes descended from Light. THE ORIGIN BEFOULED: we were found naked and smeared with muck in the roots of the Wood...'
 Shohei's preferred theories are that we are the children of apes who walked upright, although his tone here is satirical; or that we consumed not only our parents, 'which is not the Crime of the Sky', but also our origin, so that we came from Nowhere.

 自从被斯特拉思科因从布里斯托尔的一家孤儿院收养后，伊利奥波里在长达四年的时间里都是他的学生与门徒，但是他与这位严肃而神秘的绅士之间的关系总是十分复杂。他在日记中透露：“我依然认为弗雷泽是出于好意的。当然他也同意这点。但我始终无法理解他那些研究的最终目标。他也从不准备开导我。不论是否出于好意，我再也没法忍受眼之梦了。我们还算是友好地分道扬镳。”
 伊利奥波里没有完成学位课程，就在1909年离开了佩鲁贾。他早就对自己的专业失去了兴趣，日志的后半部分主要是他对翁布里亚民歌的研究，以及他对自己早期作品的注释（这些作品的质量参差不齐）。其中较好的一篇，《于黑夜的沼泽》，暗示了他曾参观过奥尔图基奥附近的古老富奇诺湖……

His journal confides: 'I still think Fraser's intentions are good. Certainly he agrees. But I never understood the final goal of his investigations. He was never prepared to enlighten me. And good intentions or not, I can no longer bear this dream of eyes. We have agreed to part, almost amicably.'
 Illopoly left Perugia in 1909 without completing his degree. He had long lost interest in his studies, and the latter half of the journal is concerned with his studies of Umbrian folk-songs, and notes towards his own compositions (which are of widely varying quality). One of the better ones, 'In the Marshes of Night', suggests he visited the site of the old Lake Fucinus near Ortucchio…

Lars Westergren, explorer and murderer, spent seven years escaping justice through his knowledge of byways and shortcuts in the Bounds. Throughout that time he wrote regularly to his daughter, possibly in part to taunt his pursuers.

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input:
Name: Perugian Diaries
Type: codex
Description: In 1907, at the age of eighteen, Christopher Illopoly left Strathcoyne's household to study theology at the University of Perugia in Italy, enrolling under the name 'Christopher Strathcoyne'.
 For four years, since his adoption from a Bristol orphanage, Illopoly served as Strathcoyne's pupil and protégé, but his relationship with this austere and secretive man was always complicated. His journal confides: 'I still think Fraser's intentions are good. Certainly he agrees. But I never understood the final goal of his investigations. He was never prepared to enlighten me. And good intentions or not, I can no longer bear this dream of eyes. We have agreed to part, almost amicably.'
 Illopoly left Perugia in 1909 without completing his degree. He had long lost interest in his studies, and the latter half of the journal is concerned with his studies of Umbrian folk-songs, and notes towards his own compositions (which are of widely varying quality). One of the better ones, 'In the Marshes of Night', suggests he visited the site of the old Lake Fucinus near Ortucchio…
output:
名称：《佩鲁贾日记》
类型：抄本
描述：1907年，十八岁的克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里离开了斯特拉思科因的宅邸，以“克里斯托弗·斯特拉思科因”之名在意大利的佩鲁贾大学学习神学。
 自从被斯特拉思科因从布里斯托尔的一家孤儿院收养后，伊利奥波里在长达四年的时间里都是他的学生与门徒，但是他与这位严肃而神秘的绅士之间的关系总是十分复杂。他在日记中透露：“我依然认为弗雷泽是出于好意的。当然他也同意这点。但我始终无法理解他那些研究的最终目标。他也从不准备开导我。不论是否出于好意，我再也没法忍受眼之梦了。我们还算是友好地分道扬镳。”
 伊利奥波里没有完成学位课程，就在1909年离开了佩鲁贾。他早就对自己的专业失去了兴趣，日志的后半部分主要是他对翁布里亚民歌的研究，以及他对自己早期作品的注释（这些作品的质量参差不齐）。其中较好的一篇，《于黑夜的沼泽》，暗示了他曾参观过奥尔图基奥附近的古老富奇诺湖……

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, preserving the solemn, ritualistic tone and occult atmosphere.
input:
名称：《建筑的诱惑》

描述：夜游术学者兼古董学家安布罗斯·威斯考特在本文中警告了“门扉的危险”，尤其着重提到了位于边境的一栋名叫“特罗文”的房子。
 “毫无疑问，他们已经开始为建造盘旋楼梯的雄心壮志而后悔；直到现今，如果有人在特罗文鲁莽地打开一扇窗，依然能不明智地看到那银色的海洋……”

Name: The Temptations of Architecture
Type: codex
Description: The antiquarian and nyctodromist Ambrose Westcott writes of the 'dangers of doors', with particular reference to a house in the bounds named 'Treowen'.
 No doubt they have come to regret the ambitions of their Winding Stair; even now in Treowen, a silver sea is unwisely visible from a rash window…'
 Westcott explains that the Wheelocks, the 'charge-holders of Treowen', have had recourse to dramatic measures to prevent oneiric encroachment, removing the entire top floor of the building. instruction: Given structured item information, generate a complete English item description.
input:
Item Info:
Name: The Geminiad ii
Type: codex
Principle: Grail: precepts of sensual desire and birth, seduction, pain, blood and thirst, hunger, greed, intoxication and delight.

Learned: Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors
Based on the information above, write a full English item description in the style of 'Book of Hours', with occult, quasi-religious and symbolic overtones.
output:
A fragile manuscript, illuminated with twinned shapes of sad and luminous beauty, and with all the phases of the moon. It might be as old as the seventh century, but the language - Fucine - is much older. The cover is a dark and exotic leather with a smooth, almost chitinous surface, decorated with jasper.
 These pages outline the seven bloody natures of the 'Daughters of Lagiah' - those corrupted immortals who gave birth to children, in defiance of the Laws of the Upper Heaven; who devoured them, in obedience to the Hours' punishment; and who have been left outside the law...
 The second volume of the Geminiad suggests that these seven corrupted immortals have been accorded the privileges of Names of the Witch-and-Sister - or perhaps the Sister-and-Witch. It reminds us that the Twins unite what is apart, and that the 'Crime of the Sky' is in some sense a supreme joining. And it speaks at length about the sadness of the seven, the sadness of mothers whose children are forever lost, and far worse than lost.

Shohei's preferred theories are that we are the children of apes who walked upright, although his tone here is satirical; or that we consumed not only our parents, 'which is not the Crime of the Sky', but also our origin, so that we came from Nowhere.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input: 名称：《伊纳姆、卡皮吉吉努皮尔、加尔基、克雷皮斯》 类型：抄本 描述：书中的四个神秘人物讲述了他们多年来在“栖木”——鸟形司辰的集会地——听到的故事。 伊纳姆：拾滩鸦没有分享他的宝藏吗？加尔基：没有分享最稀有的。他把最珍贵的留给自己了，号称那些是他找到的，不是偷来的。 卡皮吉吉努皮尔认为拾滩鸦不仅是盗贼，同时也是探子，甚至喜欢窥淫。他把司辰和祂们的具名者间秘密交合的记忆藏在居屋的角落，作为暗中夸耀的宝藏。还有一个很狂热的猜测：热情如火的林地司辰环杉，和有时与女巫做姐妹的树中牝马，这两者间有私情。

input:
名称：《王冠的胜利》

描述：一本怪书，作者署名“阿伦”。记载了某些不为人知的暗杀者们追猎和进食据称永生不死的人们的经过。出版于十九世纪后期。
 据“阿伦”称，这些暗杀者是一位名为“尚校”的神灵的使者，是“隶属于诸位秘密大师的士兵”。此类说法一直可上溯至罗马时代。
 阿伦的学识令人存疑，但是他（或是她？）的文笔简洁有力，在记述突发且暴力的死亡事件时穿插着警句：“司辰无梦，长生者力图无梦。”
output:

Type: codex
Description: Erratic accounts by 'Arun' of the hunting and consumption of supposed immortals by shadowy assassins. Published in the late nineteenth century.
 The assassins are, according to 'Arun', the agents of a power called the Coronel, a 'soldier of the Secret Masters'. The accounts date back to Roman times.

Ilse Bischoff's hallucinatory quasi-documentary, notionally about the Greco-Turkish War of the previous decade.
 A hammer-armed Turk and a sword-armed Greek pursue each other through the Pindus, setting traps for each other, robbing peasants, chalking insulting graffiti on walls. Type: book

She reportedly instructed that these secret doctrines be recorded in writing to preserve against their loss. Regrettably, the story goes, Didius Julianus ordered that the work be entombed with her in an unmarked sepulcher.

 'It is essential that these Protections be completed every fourth year, to defend against the entry of the Worms and against the avidity of the Wave and the Wound.' In the current History at least, there is no indication that these Protections have been performed regularly for at least the last thousand years.
output:
名称：《关于维持一切事物存续的教令》
类型：书籍
描述：大马士革绳结姐妹会的头领“黑色”艾丽遭到了皇帝狄第乌斯·尤利安努斯囚禁。据记载，她曾命人将这些秘密教义记录成书，以保其免于遗失，永远存续。遗憾的是，据传说狄第乌斯·尤利安努斯命人将本作随她葬入了一个没有标记的墓室。
 艾丽在本书中描述了能用于各种情况的强大保护咒。
 “重要的是，这些保护咒需每四年补修一次，以抵御蠕虫进入以及‘水波’和‘创口’的热盼。”至少在现今这重历史中，过去至少一千年内没有迹象表明有人定期施放过这些保护咒。

input:
Name: The Hissing Key

Description: An account of the ascent of the Hour called the Mother of Ants, by the Bosk-scholar Mek, of the Theban branch of the House of Lethe.
 Mek is not sympathetic to the Mother of Ants, who he calls 'the Milk-Thief'. He reviles her for her part in the death of the Seven-Coils, which he presents as a treacherous conspiracy.

 梅克并不认同蚁母——他称她为“偷奶贼”。他痛斥她参与了七蟠之死的行径，并将之描述为一场奸诈的阴谋。
 偷奶贼与丽姬亚厄客德娜、名为千夫长的准司辰（如今更常被称为“上校”）合谋，用羽毛撕裂七蟠，将她溺毙在盐中。上校因此升至司辰之位；而曾是上校女祭司的偷奶贼，因妒羡而唆使厄客德娜借予她嘶鸣之钥，从而穿过狂暴之门进入漫宿，开始她成为具名者，而终达司辰的飞升之途。

input:
Name: Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic
Type: codex
Description: Or, 'The House of Glass'. Julian Coseley considered this his masterwork.
 Techniques for perception and analysis which permit invidious and apocalyptic conclusions. Probably the most assiduously suppressed book in history. The entire run was destroyed - even the presses were melted and dispersed - but the manuscript edition has survived.
 The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. But Coseley proposes and describes 'Confinement Inescapable', aesthetic and optical techniques which might contain even an Hour, profoundly disrupting the order of the Mansus. He presents this as his own work, but there are hints here and there that he received inspiration or even assistance from the Nowhere-Hour named Snow.
output:
名称：《走近基础美学》
类型：抄本
描述：又名“镜之居屋”。朱利安·科赛利称本书为他的杰作。
 本书阐述了关于感知与分析的技巧，从中可以得出令人反感且预示着大灾变的结论。可能是历史上被查禁得最严格的书籍之一。所有的印刷本都被销毁——就连印刷机也难逃熔化与拆解的命运——但手抄版却幸存了下来。
 众司辰的完美霸权或许是永恒的。但是科赛利提出并描述了“勿逆囹圄”：一系列美学和光学技术，甚至可能做到禁锢一位司辰，这严重地威胁了漫宿的秩序。他声称本书是自己的作品，但书中的种种迹象都表明，他曾从名为白雪的虚界司辰那里得到过灵感、甚至是直接的协助。

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input: Name: Key of Night Type: codex Description: The deliberations leading to a manifesto of the 'Worms of a Scale', as recorded around 1900 in the Bar Vienna, in the cellar of the Hotel Ciervo in Noon. The Worms, all of whom use grandiose noms de guerre like Citizen Knife and the Midnight Pilgrim, agree that all previous iterations of their movement have been feckless and treacherous, and agree that the return of the prehuman Hours - the gods-from-stone - is the true way to end 'the tyranny of Eternity.' The Worms identify the Wheel, the Tide, the Flint, Sulochana, the Spider Door, the Excellency Gnathobasis and Wickel Inextinguishable as the Seven Necessary Pentiments that must be 'returned to every History through the Propaganda of the Deed'. input:
名称：《双生姝丽·卷三》
类型：抄本
描述：一本脆弱易破的手抄书，里面最引人瞩目的是一对同体孪生、光彩照人的忧郁美人形象和完整月相的图例。本书或能追溯到七世纪，而书中所用的语言——富奇诺语——则更加古老。书封面饰有珊瑚，书页边则十分锋利，足以割破咽喉。
 本书描绘了一位司辰的性质与其教义，那是一位令静止之物结合，位于水之缘、月之底的司辰：双生女巫。书中的语言暗示，神秘，错综。我需要花些时间解开它。
 《双生姝丽·卷三》提醒我们：众所周知，双生女巫常常以双生巫女的形象现身——并且当其中一面饱足时，另一面仍然可以是饥饿的。这暗示了双生女巫和林地司辰间的联系，特别是与其中一位名为丝毧的守密人的——双生女巫自己是否算作林地司辰则依旧不明。且书中用大量笔墨描绘了二位一体的悲哀，即自她们仍为血肉之躯时便留存下来的悲哀。
output:
Name: The Geminiad iii
Type: codex
Description: A fragile manuscript, illuminated with twinned shapes of sad and luminous beauty, and with all the phases of the moon. It might be as old as the seventh century, but the language - Fucine - is much older. Coral decorates its cover, and its page-edges are sharp enough to slash a throat.
 These pages outline the nature, and the doctrines, of an Hour that demands the union of what has been separated, an Hour that is sought at the water's edge and beneath the moon: the Witch-and-Sister. The language is allusive, enigmatic, intricate. It'll take some untangling.
 The third volume of the Geminiad reminds us that the Witch-and-Sister has been known to manifest as the Sister-and-Witch - and that this face may heal, while the other face is always hungry. It implies connections between the Witch-and-Sister and the Hours of the Wood - especially the secret-keeper called the Velvet - but it is ambiguous on whether the Witch-and-Sister is a Wood-hour proper. And it speaks at length about the sadness of the two-who-are-one, the sadness that remains from their time as flesh.

In the early 1530s, the last Abbot of St Brandan's, called 'Roaring Richard', set down his conversations with the illiterate local cunning-man, Red William.
 Red William describes the seven forms in which he 'goes about and under the world' - viper, cat, fox, eagle, dove, boar and crow. Abbot Richard ingeniously fits these all into a framework of Solar belief…
 According to Abbot Richard, each of Red William's forms is closer to the Sun, and is increasingly 'winged with virtue'. Richard draws an analogy with the waxen wings of Icarus: hypocrisy and false virtue will melt before the Sun's heat, and so sincerity and untrammelled expression of the Self are the utmost piety. It's worth noting that only a year or two after Richard wrote this book, John Tregonwell was so appalled by the debaucheries of the monks of St Brandan's that he recommended the monastery's immediate dissolution.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, preserving the solemn, ritualistic tone and occult atmosphere.
input:
名称：《为王着迷》
类型：抄本
描述：本书详细记录了作者在南欧、埃及和安纳托利亚的坟场与墓地中看到的秘密欢宴和迷醉之舞。作者其人坦白了自己是食尸鬼，啃食土中尸体的生物：他称自己在大快朵颐时见到了书中的舞蹈。
 这套舞蹈源自祭奉女神伊西斯与库柏勒的密教所传承的奥秘，不仅含有象征和实际意义上的剥皮行为，而且永远以人类心脏为仪式的主轴。作者着重圈点了他对自己被打断的宴席的令人作呕的感官描写。
 “在那些盛大宴席期间，总有一头黑猪在经受屠宰前被加冕为王。每逢此时，它的心脏会经天平与一片羽毛互较轻重，而它的皮会成为主祭的披风。它的血肉被留给乌鸦，但我必须坦白我意不在其尸骸，而在于女帽制造者新入土的喷了香水的肉体。”
output:
Name: Rapt in the King
Type: codex
Description: Detailed accounts of secret bacchanals and ecstatic dances observed in necropolises and graveyards in Southern Europe, in Egypt and in Anatolia. The author is a self-confessed ghoul, an eater of buried flesh: he claims to have witnessed the dances while at his feasting.
 The dances draw from the traditions of the Mysteries, of the cults of Isis and of Cybele, but include both symbolic and literal flayings, and the human heart is always central in the rites. The author punctuates his accounts with queasily sensuous descriptions of his own interrupted feasts.
 'At these greater Feasts a Black Pig is always crowned as King before its Slaying. On this Occasion, its Heart was weighed in the Balance against a Knot of Feathers, and its Skin became a Cape for the Officiant. Its Flesh was left for the Crows, but I must confess my Interest was not in its Carcass but in the Perfumed Flesh of the Milliner laid fresh in the Earth.'

It implies connections between the Witch-and-Sister and the Hours of the Wood - especially the secret-keeper called the Velvet - but it is ambiguous on whether the Witch-and-Sister is a Wood-hour proper. input: 名称：《他者的对白》 类型：抄本 描述：萨缪尔·萨维奇最具思想性的作品之一：一部关于“明晰”城里的讽喻剧，这座城市本身也是一本书，同时又是书里的句子。 “谚语”勋爵与“学术”勋爵在“明晰”的街头爆发了战争，与此同时，其他“标点”们则醉饮墨水，讲着各种笑话（虽然就萨维奇一贯的标准来说，这些笑话并不算多）。 剧本的最后一幕是“谚语”勋爵打开“明晰”的城门，把所有人驱逐到了未知之处。（剧中角色用于开门时的法术是真实存在的——将“阈前格律”与启一起使用，可创造出具有力量的门关符印。）

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input: 名称：《努列尔宝训集》 类型：书籍 描述：集结成册的绳结姐妹会教喻；该秘传默观修会存在于每一重历史，且在某些重历史中拥有莫大的力量。本书由署名“努列尔”者编集，是致圣特里丰的献礼。 努列尔解释说，圣特里丰以“流血与出产的她”和“开启的她”之名展现了隐秘的奇迹。圣特里丰于是开启了通往太阳居屋的道路；圣特里丰于是经由“伟大生诞”，飞升成为不死之人。 圣特里丰的飞升始于他穿过“双角之门”。他随后学习了“酩酊祷文”——此文因极度神圣而未被努列尔录于此书。且努列尔严厉地解释说，为了获得“伟大生诞”的七道印记，圣特里丰摄食了“不仅有灵魂已逝之人，还有灵魂犹存之人。”
output:
Name: The Rose of Nuriel
Type: book
Description: A volume of collected teachings of the Sisterhood of the Knot, that arcane-contemplative order that existed in all histories, but in some was very powerful indeed. This was recorded by 'Nuriel', and dedicated to St Tryphon.
 St Tryphon, Nuriel explains, performed secret miracles in the name of 'She who Bleeds and Bears' and 'She who Opens'. Thus St Tryphon opened the way to the House of the Sun; thus St Tryphon underwent the Great Birth, an ascension to immortality.
 St Tryphon began his ascension by passing the 'Horned Door'. He continued it by learning the 'Invocation Thiatic' - which Nuriel does not here record, on account of its extreme holiness. And, Nuriel explains grimly, to achieve the Seven Marks of the Great Birth, St Tryphon consumed 'both those whose soul had left them, and even those in whom the soul remained.'

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《日出的觉醒》
类型：抄本
描述：一份犀利的非典型沉思录，作者系刃之长生者，梅里昂郡的图瓦格。他日后用许多化名拜访过噤声居屋，通常是为了寻求某种战斗。
 “若光有声，它就会变成音乐。若音乐可见，它就会变成光……”
 图瓦格认为，每天的光都被过去每天的光轻抚；所以通过当下每天的光，我们或许能够开始认识到未来会发生的事。至少，这似乎是他得出的结论，但文章却在此戛然而止，显然是他对这个主题失去了兴趣，亦或是遭受了某人的伏击。
output:
Name: Sunrise Awakenings
Type: codex
Description: An uncharacteristically poignant meditation by the Edge-long Twrog of Meirionnydd, who later came to Hush House under a variety of other names, often in search of some sort of fight.
 'If Light were not silent, it would be Music. If Music were visible, it would be Light…'
 Each day's light, Twrog suggests, is faintly touched by the light of every past day; so in the light of every present day, we may begin to understand something of days to come. At least, this appears to be his conclusion, but he stops in mid-sentence, apparently having lost patience with the act of writing, or possibly been ambushed.

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持阴郁庄严、带有神秘主义与宗教神话色彩的文风。
input:
Name: Velletri Interviews
Type: record
Description: Interrogation of a man named Lacombe, a former Nocturnal Branch inspector now identified as 'terminally robigoid'.
 Lacombe is not especially lucid, and the state called 'robigoia' evidently includes a malady of the lungs which causes coughing fits: he weakens audibly over the course of the interrogation. He is questioned about the disposition of various unsanctioned items recovered from a Nocturnal Branch raid on a castle at Ortucchio, in the region of the Fucine Marshes. He is, however, defiant as well as incoherent.
 Lacombe insists the items have been put to good use; he derides Nocturnal Branch as 'the lackeys of Calyptra'. Alarmingly, during the last few minutes of the interrogation, he begins to insist that his interrogator should 'burn the Library'. He waxes enthusiastic about the fire he wants to see, leading to a final coughing fit after which the interview abruptly ends.
output:
名称：《韦莱特里审讯记录》
类型：唱片
描述：对一个名为拉孔布的男人的审讯记录，此人曾任夜勤处的督察，如今则被认定是“晚期罗比戈症患者”。
 拉孔布并不是特别清醒，所谓的“罗比戈症”显然包括某种导致咳嗽的肺部症状。在审讯过程中，他的声音越来越弱。他被质询了对各种未经批准物品的处理情况，这些物品是夜勤处在对位于富奇诺沼泽地区，奥尔图基奥的一座城堡的突击搜查中缴获的。然而，他既态度挑衅，又语无伦次。
 拉孔布坚称，那些物品都得到了妥善的利用；他还嘲笑夜勤处是“根冠的走狗”。令人不安的是，在审讯的最后几分钟，他开始坚持审讯者应该“烧掉图书馆”。他对自己想看到的那股火焰充满狂热，这导致了一阵剧烈的咳嗽，审讯在此戛然而止。

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《逃亡者信笺集》
类型：信件
描述：探险家及杀人犯拉尔斯·韦斯特格伦曾在七年的时间里，利用他对边境上的小路与边门的了解躲避追捕。在那段时间里，他曾定期给自己的女儿写信——兴许也是为了嘲讽他的追兵们。
 韦斯特格伦曾在门关军团服役一年，巡逻边境，直至叛逃；在莫尔比昂的船长修道院躲了一个月；还在波涛之下的伊苏住了七天（至少他如此声称）……
 在最终被追兵逼得走投无路的时候，韦斯特格伦写道，他将“尝试日之道途”。他对自己的冒险行为似乎也不怎么乐观，事实上，这是他的最后一封信。编者在最后补充说，韦斯特格伦的下落与结局依然不明，尽管据说有人在1929年维也纳的“圣诞集市”上见过他——那是无形世界的黑帮人物们每年举办的洽谈会。
output:
Name: Letters from a Fugitive
Type: letter
Description: Lars Westergren, explorer and murderer, spent seven years escaping justice through his knowledge of byways and shortcuts in the Bounds. Throughout that time he wrote regularly to his daughter, possibly in part to taunt his pursuers.
 A year with the Légion du Seuil, patrolling the Bounds, until he deserts; a month in the Priory of Captains in Morbihan; seven days, or so he claims, in Ys behind the wave…
 Cornered at last by his pursuers, Westergren writes that he will 'attempt the Paths of the Sun'. He doesn't seem sanguine about his chances, and indeed, this is his last letter. An editor's note adds that Westergren's whereabouts or end remain unknown, although he was supposedly sighted at the 'Christmas Market' in Vienna - the negotiations between invisible underworld figures that happen each year there - in 1929.

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input:
Name: Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903
Type: codex
Description: A confidential journal kept by Greene, former Nocturnal Branch Superindent but, by 1903, Librarian of the House. Greene has kept his journal in Hyksos, presumably as an extra measure of privacy.
 In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'
 The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau... 

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.
output:
名称：《大卫·格林爵士的日志·1903》
类型：抄本
描述：格林写的一本机密日志，他曾是夜勤处的警司，并于1903年就任居屋的图书管理员一职。格林用希克索斯语写了这本日志，大概是为了极端地保护他的隐私。
 1903年，居屋和夜勤处合作密切，而格林则是这场合作明面上的代言人。然而，显然格林私底下对夜勤处失望至极，他愈发认为其没有履行好职责。他对建造在布兰库格监狱下方的“镇压装置”尤为担忧。
“司辰和具名者都很危险，”他写道，“但至少我们应对祂们的措施都建立在长期的经验之上。但这样一位司辰：行动早于诞生之神——自从未进入之处离去之神——如果她的具名者行于世间，我们要如何才能了解祂们的能力与行动方式？”
 交替出现的算式（潮汐，日期，财务测算）和对“A·F”的热望的表述组成了日志最后的记录。格林似乎打算带着A·F远走高飞，其中有些算式表明，他一直以来都在挪用资金，奥尔图基奥事件及随后夜勤处重组为防剿局时的混乱局面为其提供了掩护……然而，这些记录在这年结束前便戛然而止。格林是否真的带着这些资金与挚友潜逃，以及他是否出于其他原因丢弃了这本日志，均不明了。

input: Name: De Horis book 3 Type: codex Description: In Latin. This is usually described as the third volume of 'De Horis', but Darcy-Evers' foreword argues persuasively that it's a substantial reworking by the original author… The Lionsmith makes monsters, the Colonel has his scars, but the De Horis now insists that neither can truly defeat the other; that they must at some level understand these limits in their strategies; and that their enmity is an 'eternal engine of the world.'

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持阴郁庄严、带有神秘主义与宗教神话色彩的文风。
input:
Name: Ud Rocashaas
Type: codex
Description: An anonymous confessional account of unsanctioned activities by the nuns of St Brandan's. The title is a Henavek phrase that might be translated as 'the spirit flees the shadowed places.'
 The author writes guiltily of her dealings with hill-children and Carapace-relics - she suggests she herself has a connection with one of the Carapace-kinds. Most of these dealings are trivial, but she claims to have arranged the death of the Marcher Lord William de Braose, called Black William...
 De Braose' wife, Eva, evidently seeks the Abbey's help to free her from her hated husband. Subsequently he is found in the bed-chamber of the wife of Llywelyn the Great, Prince of the Welsh, while attempting to negotiate the marriage of his daughter (also Eva) to Llywelyn's son. Llywellyn takes this badly, de Braose is hanged, the elder Eva inherits his estates and makes a substantial endowment to St Brandan's. In the author's telling, de Braose was 'innocent of all but cruelty' and the adulterer found in the bed-chamber was a shape-changing 'undergoer'...
output:
名称：Ud Rocashaas
类型：抄本
描述：一本匿名的忏悔录，记录了圣布伦丹的修女们所做的未经批准的行为。标题是一个赫沃尔语短句，可以翻译成“心灵逃离覆影之地”。
 作者语带歉疚地写到她与丘陵之子和介壳遗族的交易——她暗示自己仍与介壳种的某个种群保持联系。这些交易大多无关紧要，但她声称是自己筹划了边地领主威廉·德·布劳斯的死亡，即人称“黑威廉”的那位……
 德·布劳斯的妻子，伊娃，显然曾向修道院寻求帮助，好摆脱她那烦人的丈夫。随后，他就在威尔士亲王卢埃林妻子的卧室里被捉奸在床，当时布劳斯正在筹划女儿（也名叫伊娃）与卢埃林儿子的婚事。卢埃林勃然大怒，把德·布劳斯绞死了。年长的那位伊娃继承了布劳斯的财产，并向圣布伦丹修道院捐赠了一笔巨款。在作者的叙述中，德·布劳斯“除了残忍之外，在这件事里清清白白”，卧室里的通奸者只是个易形的“衾下魅”……

 “向大地低声吐露你的秘密，用火将它们烧毁，弃至海中。即便如此，它们依然会紧抓你的头发”，密续如此提醒道。它给出了一个密教谜语，称其有时能解答猎手之门的谜语。

instruction: 将下面的英文文本翻译为中文，保持原作的神秘主义与哲思感，并保留隐喻与象征的味道。
input: Birth occurs at the conjunction of pleasure and torment. So the first Forbidden Acts of the Forge birthed sparks of delight which took root in the Glory or in Nowhere: who can say? So the seeds of the Flowermaker were planted, though for long years he was nothing but an unfulfilled ache.
output: 分娩发生于欢愉与苦痛结合之时。因而铸炉的第一条禁忌行径诞下欢欣的火花，于辉光或虚界生根发芽：谁又能肯定在哪呢？因而制花人的种子埋下，尽管在很长的年月里他只是一处无法满足的期盼。

input:
Name: The Temptations of Architecture
Type: codex
Description: The antiquarian and nyctodromist Ambrose Westcott writes of the 'dangers of doors', with particular reference to a house in the bounds named 'Treowen'.
 No doubt they have come to regret the ambitions of their Winding Stair; even now in Treowen, a silver sea is unwisely visible from a rash window…'
 Westcott explains that the Wheelocks, the 'charge-holders of Treowen', have had recourse to dramatic measures to prevent oneiric encroachment, removing the entire top floor of the building. 'Nevertheless,' he writes, 'the business of the Moon-Hall has begun to touch the other business of the house...'
output:
名称：《建筑的诱惑》
类型：抄本
描述：夜游术学者兼古董学家安布罗斯·威斯考特在本文中警告了“门扉的危险”，尤其着重提到了位于边境的一栋名叫“特罗文”的房子。
 “毫无疑问，他们已经开始为建造盘旋楼梯的雄心壮志而后悔；直到现今，如果有人在特罗文鲁莽地打开一扇窗，依然能不明智地看到那银色的海洋……”
 威斯考特解释说，作为“特罗文的管理人”，惠洛克家族不得不采取一系列夸张的措施来阻止梦境侵蚀，以至于拆除了整个房屋的顶楼。“尽管如此，”他补充道，“月厅已经开始对房屋内的其他事物施以影响……”

 亨利的“大不幸”——他在长枪比武中受的重伤——让他从此无法站得“比折断的柳条更直”……
 嘲弄中最为刻薄的部分针对的是亨利的“大贬质”，他软化金属上的腐败已蔓延到了王国的货币中。最后也是最严肃的一篇讽刺诗煽动性地提及了“熔炉革命”。
output:
Name: Old Coppernose and the Softer Metal
Type: codex
Description: A disgraceful compendium of ribald poetry about the habits and corruptions of Henry VIII.
 Henry's 'Great Misfortune' - his crushing injury at a jousting bout - has left him unable to stand 'any straighter than a splintered withy'…
 The most savage mockery is reserved for Henry's 'Great Debasement', where the corruption of his softer metal is supposed to have crept into the coin of the realm. The last and most serious lampoon makes seditious references to 'the Crucible Revolution'.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《苍白女士与葡萄酒王子》
类型：抄本
描述：一本关于末代德沃尔夫，伊娃·德沃尔夫的匿名传记，本书更关注她的个人困扰与私密恋情。
 伊娃·德沃尔夫和亚伯拉罕·惠洛克订了婚，他却在婚礼祭坛前毁约，将她抛弃。伊娃在羞耻与愤怒之中回到了布兰库格，再也没有出现在伦敦。她离开三天后，亚伯拉罕·惠洛克的尸体被冲上了格雷夫森德的海岸。他的面部被群鸟啄食得面目全非，只能通过随身物体来辨认——其中包括一封烫有漆印的、寄给惠洛克的信，信的内容似乎表明他是奥地利人雇佣的间谍。后续调查显示信件似乎系伪造，但事件的全貌依然不甚明了……
 富兰克林·班克罗夫特勋爵，有时也被称为葡萄酒王子，他对布兰库格庄园进行过一系列的造访。他与伊娃的关系逐渐成为了丑闻的源头。伊娃当时已经四十九岁，但关于德沃尔夫与班克罗夫特所生后嗣的传言却多年不绝。这本传记的作者声称，在伊娃“投水而死”之前，她与班克罗夫特所生的孩子已经被她的朋友骚赛夫妇收养——这个孩子成为了日后的桂冠诗人罗伯特·骚赛的姊妹（此说法并无实证）。
output:
Name: A Pale Lady and a Prince of Wines
Type: codex
Description: An anonymous biography of Eva Dewulf, last of the Dewulfs, focused rather salaciously on her personal troubles and intrigues.
 Eva Dewulf is engaged to one Abraham Wheelock, but he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again. Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. These include a waxed pouch containing a letter addressed to Wheelock, whose contents seem to show he is a spy in the pay of the Austrians. Subsequent investigations suggest that the letter is a forgery, but the matter remains obscure...
 Lord Franklin Bancroft, sometimes called the Prince of Wines, begins a series of visits to Brancrug House. His relationship with Eva becomes a source of scandal. Eva is by now forty-nine, but rumours persist for years of a Dewulf-Bancroft heir. Eva's biographer claims that before her 'drowning death', her child by Bancroft was adopted by her friends the Southeys - that the child became the sister of the later Poet Laureate, Robert Southey. (No real evidence is provided in support of this claim.)

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input:
Name: Two Wombs, One Heart
Type: codex
Description: A fanciful account by Thirza Blake of the early life of the Twins - their time as mortals before they became Hours or even Long, in a 'dry kingdom beyond the Western Sea' which Thirza suggests might have been ancient Mexico.
 'It is widely known that the Sister was rich and the Witch poor. It is widely known that the Witch loved the Sister first. It is not widely known that the Witch was first employed to teach the Sister the arts of embroidery…'
 Although Thirza is very probably just making up much of the story, there are long passages expounding notable techniques of weave-work and thread-feit. In particular, when Witch and Sister flee across the Sea to be together, Thirza explains how they fashioned a 'peace-weave' with Heart and these arts, and then, to tame the winds, called on Heart again to swaddle the thunder in the peace-weave.
output: 名称：《两个子宫，一颗心脏》 类型：抄本 描述：蒂尔扎·布雷克对孪生子的早期经历的想象性描述，远在她们成为司辰，甚至长生者之前；那时她们还作为凡人生活在“西海彼岸的干燥王国”，蒂尔扎认为那可能就是古墨西哥。 “众所周知，巫女富有，女巫贫穷。同样众所周知的是女巫先爱上了巫女。而鲜为人知的是：女巫先受雇教授巫女刺绣的技艺……” 尽管这些故事的大部分内容可能都是蒂尔扎杜撰的，但本书确实有相当的篇幅阐述了值得注意的、有关编织和穿线的技术。尤其是在描写女巫和巫女为了厮守而横渡大海的桥段时，蒂尔扎讲解了她们是如何通过心与这些技艺编织出“平息之网”，以及为了驯服风暴，她们如何再次唤起心，用平息之网裹住了雷霆。

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:

类型：抄本
描述：在无影众王时代，恩尼斯·拉扎里因预言太阳的分裂而被处以极刑。若抓捕他的人日后长成了长生者，现在大概会感到惭愧。
 拉扎里称太阳将在锤炼场被白日铸炉分裂，后者的凶器是心中的爱。
 “导致太阳之死的不会是爱，而是妒忌。导致太阳之死的不会是妒忌，而是渴求。导致太阳之死必不是渴求，而是好奇。置他于死地的必不是好奇，终究还是爱。”

Type: codex

 Lazali indicates that the Sun will be divided in the Malleary, by the Forge of Days, armed with the love in her heart.
 'Love will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather envy. Envy will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather thirst. Thirst shall not be the cause of his death, but curiosity. Curiosity shall not be his end; rather will it be love.'

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input: 名称：《七大碎片》 类型：抄本 描述：作为司掌斗争的两位伟大司辰之一，狮子匠曾将他的佩剑碎为七片。噤声居屋的第五任图书管理员，纳塔莉娅·布鲁洛夫以寓言及其他形式描述了每一块碎片的特性。 “于是第三碎片被定义为‘痛苦悲鸣’。狮子匠是位坚忍的司辰，但我们不得不推测，即便是他也无法在分离之刻抑制自己的痛苦。如今我们把锡在重压下发出的声音称之为‘锡鸣’——恐怕这就是把第三碎片进一步命名为‘王者碎片’的原因……” “我们将第七碎片非正式地称作无敌勇莽，它能从致胜之着中崩出，如同致胜之着从回忆中崩出——只要运用足够的刃。”
output:
Name: Seven Shards
Type: codex
Description: The Lionsmith, one of the two great Hours of struggle, broke his sword into seven shards. Natalia Brulleau, fifth Librarian of Hush House, describes the nature of each of those shards, allegorically and otherwise.
 'The Third Shard then has been identified with 'the cry of pain'. The Lionsmith is a stoic Hour, but we must assume that in the Sundering Moment even he might have been unable to restrain his distress. Now the sound of tin under pressure we call the 'tin cry' - a reason, perhaps, for the further identification of the Third Shard as the 'Shard Royal'...
 'The Seventh Shard we call, informally, the Invincible Audacity, which is struck from the Winning Move as the Winning Move is struck from a memory - with the application of sufficient Edge.'

input: 名称：《费克里的草药学》 类型：抄本 描述：埃桑·费克里的早期作品，早在他担任岛屿决议会的护理理事之前，那时他还是一名旅行治疗师。 作为剑齿兽，埃桑只吃在土地中找到的东西，所以他最擅长根之秘传…… 埃桑在康沃尔的海滩边发现了一种白色的水草，可作为引相与冬相的实用来源。写到这段时，他的语气似乎有些负罪感——或许是因为他竟然对海产表现出了兴趣，而这对剑齿兽来说是不明智的；抑或是因为他建议把这一物种命名为“伊娃华发”，暗示他对布兰库格的苍白女士有些许好感……
output:
Name: Fekri's Herbary
Type: codex
Description: The early wisdom of Ehsan Fekri, at that point a travelling healer, much later the Secretary Salvant of the Curia of the Isle.
 As a skaptodon, Ehsan may consume only that which is found in the earth, so he's best with root-lore...
 Ehsan identifies a pale sea-weed found on the beaches of Cornwall as a useful source of Rose and Winter aspect. His tone here is a little guilty - perhaps because he's showing an interest in sea-produce, which might be thought unwise for a skaptodon, and perhaps because his proposal to name it 'Eva's Locks' suggests a tiny crush on the Pale Lady of Brancrug...

 格里高利显然成功地开辟了一条通往他所谓“月厅”的通道，但在那之后，他的叙述逐渐越发混乱。他坚称在月厅内双角斧依然是一位刃之神明；他希望能有一个“永恒的对手”，但未能找到。后期的记述中越来越多地穿插着象棋记步的符号，最终戛然而止。

 Gregory evidently succeeds in opening a way to something he calls the 'Moon-Hall', but here his account becomes erratic. He insists that in the Moon-Hall the Horned-Axe is still an Edge-power; he hopes for an 'eternal rival', but cannot find the one he needs. output: Eva Dewulf is engaged to one Abraham Wheelock, but he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again. Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. Name: The Geminiad ii
Type: codex
Description: A fragile manuscript, illuminated with twinned shapes of sad and luminous beauty, and with all the phases of the moon.  The second volume of the Geminiad suggests that these seven corrupted immortals have been accorded the privileges of Names of the Witch-and-Sister - or perhaps the Sister-and-Witch. It reminds us that the Twins unite what is apart, and that the 'Crime of the Sky' is in some sense a supreme joining. And it speaks at length about the sadness of the seven, the sadness of mothers whose children are forever lost, and far worse than lost.

input: 名称：《心之乐器》 类型：抄本 描述：时任圣布伦丹修道院女领唱一职的伊莎贝尔修女，与一名位列“叩心魅”的心之长生者间进行的对谈。后者当时已部分占据了她的身体。 就像它的所有同类那样，叩心魅通常居住在漫宿中，但也能够以音乐的形式进入物质世界，并占据一个自愿（或是半自愿）的听到并喜爱那种音乐的凡人的身体……比如伊莎贝尔。 伊莎贝尔记录了她在漫宿的高处所见的梦境——在那里她被暂时赋予了叩心魅的头衔与地位。作为回报，叩心魅在物质世界享受着它所谓的“音顿”——一种无拘无束的混沌状态。“我们最大的幸事便是我们永不休止——除了在音顿之中。”伊莎贝尔还提到了一种她称之为“强音顿”的概念，但她也哀叹，她的叩心魅不会告诉她那具体是什么。

Ilse Bischoff's bewildering, widely derided final film.
 The film is an unrelenting fusillade of apparently unrelated images - birth, mirrors, grain-threshers, animal attacks, crowds at stations… but a single image appears again and again, dominating the rush of images until the film is only a single static shot.
 The repeating image is a view through a grimy window-pane of a nearby tower. There is a vague impression of flickering light around the tower-top. Just as the film ends, smoke plumes from the tower. That's it. Description: A manual of the Ordo Limiae, an order of quasi-immortals who maintained a secret enclave at the source of the river Limia, in the Roman province of Hispania Gallaecia. This manual was compiled by one Kurenai, who claims to have fled 'the tyranny of the Chrysanthemum Throne' to cross the world and join the Ordo.
 Members of the Ordo took an oath, the Ivory Chain, not to have commerce with the Hours. Followed literally, this would be almost impossible for an adept, so the manual contains numerous clarifications, exceptions and processes of indulgence.
 Kurenai describes the Order's burial rites, which include spells to ensure - in theory - that the souls of dead Long are not given to the Hours. The Hour called the Ivory Dove, who memorialises and commemorates, is to be invoked, in secret, in these rites, 'for with that Hour we have made an understanding'.

名称：《白骨之书》
类型：书籍

 教团成员必须许下名为“白骨锁链”的誓言，保证不与司辰做交易。对一名学徒来说，要一字一句遵守这个誓言几乎是不可能的，因此指南书中收录了不计其数的解释、例外和赦罪办法。
 作者红描述了教团的葬礼仪式，其中包括能够——理论上——确保不将逝去长生者的灵魂交给司辰的咒语。此类仪式会隐秘地向回忆与纪念之神——名为骨白鸽的司辰致以祈求，“因我们与那位司辰达成了共识。”

Type: book
Description: A play dealing with the nine-year sojourn of a snow-goddess in the Thracian city of Abydos, by 'Apollo Fireweaver'. It enjoyed success in London in its 1892 edition, when it was republished from - apparently - an older Greek text.
 The entity called 'Chione' arrives in a blizzard and demands the city gates are barred. As Abydos falls under her spell, the dead return, but do not speak...
 For eight years the city is a place of slow death, frosty ecstasy and silent beauty, but in the ninth year a Conspiracy of Shouts is mounted against the quiet that Chione demands. The conspirators open the city gates, and a scarred man comes to drag Chione out by the hair. Summer returns, but the conspirators die of remorse.

 一个名为“喀俄涅”的存在于暴风雪中降临，要求紧闭城门。随着阿拜多斯城陷落于她的咒语，死者苏生回归，却闭口不言……

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《喀俄涅在阿拜多斯城》
类型：书籍
描述：一部以白雪女神在色雷斯的阿拜多斯城逗留九年为题材的戏剧，作者署名“阿波罗·织火者”。本剧的1892年版本在伦敦大获成功，该版本——似乎——是在那一年从更加古老的希腊语文本转译而来的。
 一个名为“喀俄涅”的存在于暴风雪中降临，要求紧闭城门。随着阿拜多斯城陷落于她的咒语，死者苏生回归，却闭口不言……
 八年间，这座城市充斥着缓慢的死亡、霜冻的迷醉与沉默的美。但到了第九年，一场“呐喊谋反”发起，意在颠覆喀俄涅所要求的静寂。谋反者打开城门，放一个身负伤疤的男人前来拽住喀俄涅的头发将她拖出城外。炎夏复又回返，而谋反者们却死于悔恨。
output:
Name: Chione at Abydos
Type: book
Description: A play dealing with the nine-year sojourn of a snow-goddess in the Thracian city of Abydos, by 'Apollo Fireweaver'. It enjoyed success in London in its 1892 edition, when it was republished from - apparently - an older Greek text.
 The entity called 'Chione' arrives in a blizzard and demands the city gates are barred. As Abydos falls under her spell, the dead return, but do not speak...
 For eight years the city is a place of slow death, frosty ecstasy and silent beauty, but in the ninth year a Conspiracy of Shouts is mounted against the quiet that Chione demands. The conspirators open the city gates, and a scarred man comes to drag Chione out by the hair. Summer returns, but the conspirators die of remorse.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, keeping a gothic, symbol-laden style reminiscent of esoteric literature.
input: “雅努斯是守门者、双面之神、制造伤口之神、昭示改变之神，是太阳，是月亮。所以我们视他作守夜人、孪生子、蚁母、铸炉、弧月和昕旦。他不可能兼为上述诸神吧？这可能吗？古罗马祭司们了解教堂，了解干涸之地，了解埃拉伽巴路斯。所以他是杂糅而成的吗？亦或他是其他存在？在加拉埃西亚，人们称他为亚努斯·拉弥俄斯，不过忘却会是人尽皆知地爱好诽谤，此名不可全信。”
output: 'Janus is the Gatekeeper, the twin-god, the god that wounds, the presager of changes, the sun, the moon. So we identify him with the Watchman, the Twins, with the Mother, with the Forge, with the Meniscate and the Madrugad. He cannot be all these. Can he? The flamines knew the Church, knew the Dry Land, knew Elagabalus. Is he then synthesis? Or is he something else? In Gallaecia they called him Ianus Lamius, but the Obliviates are notorious for their slanders.'

 'It is not now widely believed that the sons and daughters of the Red Rose were forged into immortals. Understandably: they are, after all, now all long dead. The Forge itself devoured the greatest among them.'
 The royalty of England, according to Willis-Ford, became the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame, destroying or transforming their enemies, conquering Europe, establishing grand cathedrals to St Spark. The alliance with the Forge begins to take its toll. At last, the Bronze King undergoes his 'Great Misfortune' and 'Great Debasement', and is afterwards known as the Copper King. 类型：抄本

 “如今，人们已经普遍不相信红玫瑰家族的儿女们曾经被铸造为不朽者。这倒是可以理解：毕竟，他们早已全都化为白骨。铸炉自己吞噬了他们中的最伟大者。”

Description: An anonymous erotic novel occasionally claimed to have been written by Eva Dewulf, although at least two duels were fought in her honour to avenge this slander.
 The novel graphically details Madame Ettery's various imprisonments, ravishments and escapes in the debauched Commonwealth of Tinctures and its neighbour, the pious Atrament.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, preserving its restrained but unsettling, myth-tinged tone.
input: 交替出现的算式（潮汐，日期，财务测算）和对“A·F”的热望的表述组成了日志最后的记录。格林似乎打算带着A·F远走高飞，其中有些算式表明，他一直以来都在挪用资金，奥尔图基奥事件及随后夜勤处重组为防剿局时的混乱局面为其提供了掩护……然而，这些记录在这年结束前便戛然而止。格林是否真的带着这些资金与挚友潜逃，以及他是否出于其他原因丢弃了这本日志，均不明了。
output:
The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau... 

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《聚点日记》
类型：书籍
描述：探险家及杀人犯拉尔斯·韦斯特格伦的日记。不巧的是，他为了防人耳目将其翻译成了弗里吉亚语。
 “世界上存在地图，存在传说，存在蕴含传说的地图，与有关地图的传说。漫宿的面相存于所有这些之中，如同水存于沼泽、杯盏与天空中。”
 韦斯特格伦描述了一系列漫宿内的探险。他着重于冒险经历的种种细节——色彩，景色，质感——而不是实际行为。他的确警告说漫宿每年都在变化，不过也像读者了保证门扉一直不变。“那些门也许会关合，但永远不会消失。起码有凡人留在漫宿时如此。我们在这儿就像老鼠。”
output:
Name: The Concursum Diaries
Type: book
Description: The diaries of the explorer and murderer Lars Westergren. He's unhelpfully translated them into Phrygian, for privacy.
 'There are map-legends, there are maps of legends, and there are legends of maps. Aspects of the Mansus subsist in all of these, in much the same way that you find water in a swamp and in a cup and in the sky.'
 Westergren describes a series of expeditions into the Mansus. He focuses on the details of the experience - the colours, the vistas, the textures - rather than the practicalities. He does warn that the Mansus changes each year, although he assures the reader that the Doors have been the same. 'Doors may close, but they never disappear. At least not while there have been mortals in the Mansus. We're like mice.'

Type: codex
Description: This was probably the 'prophecies of the naga' rendered into English, and illustrated, by 'William Midnight' in Paris in the 1880s; but it shows a number of divergences from that text. It's certainly quite recent by the standards of Vak texts.
 The serpent-folk called the Great Hooded Princes came to know the order called the House of Lethe, and warred across the miles with them. They made an alliance with the Mother of Ants, 'whose children they had been'...

input:
Name: Singlefoot Songs
Type: codex
Description: Father Stanislav John Schaller, priest and diplomat, writes of his time on the slopes of Huashan - 'near to the Grove of the Green Immortals, but never too near.'
 Schaller's relations with the Grove are cautious - it's a Library of the Tree, but under the hand of the Hour named Applebright. In time, however, Schaller comes to be more sympathetic to the Applebright, which he suggests 'causes harm only when so invited.'
 The 'Singlefoots' of the title are one-horned, one-footed hill-things with sweet but powerful voices - powerful enough to 'open the mountain.' The Singlefoots sometimes trample pilgrims; sometimes heal them; sometimes coerce them to 'enter the mountain' and become Singlefoots. output:
名称：《夔牛之歌》
类型：抄本
描述：外交官兼教士斯坦尼斯拉夫·约翰·沙勒神父写下了他在华山山麓度过的时光——“可以靠近翠仙苑，但别靠太近。”
 沙勒在处理和林苑的关系时表现得十分谨慎——它是树的图书馆，却处于名为光明果的司辰掌控之下。不过，随着时间的推移，沙勒开始逐渐理解光明果，认为光明果“只在受邀时有害”。

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, preserving the solemn, ritualistic tone and occult atmosphere.
input: 名称：《遭掠的世界》 类型：抄本 描述：副标题为“荒野中的花朵”：一本以寓言形式呈现医学论述的史诗。作者是第五代布兰库格男爵基甸·德沃尔夫，他有时也被刻薄地称作“切割者”。 本书的韵诗部分基于渔夫王的传说，但进行了大量的改编。一位荒原的受伤君王得知他与他的土地可以被治愈，但疗法是将把他们引向更加野蛮的病态行径…… 基甸在最后举了个具体的应用范例：书中的奥秘可以用来掠夺“吾之浸液”，但若是唤起足够的心，就能将它进一步提炼为“舞动之血”。

 The poem is a substantial variation on the Fisher-King tale. A wounded wasteland monarch learns that he and his land can be cured, but that the cure is their own response to ever more savage maladies…
 Gideon concludes with a concrete example: that the Mysteries can be used to despoil 'mine own Soaks', but then the Soak can then be refined with sufficient Heart into 'the sanguis saltandis'.

 “雅努斯是守门者、双面之神、制造伤口之神、昭示改变之神，是太阳，是月亮。所以我们视他作守夜人、孪生子、蚁母、铸炉、弧月和昕旦。他不可能兼为上述诸神吧？这可能吗？古罗马祭司们了解教堂，了解干涸之地，了解埃拉伽巴路斯。所以他是杂糅而成的吗？亦或他是其他存在？在加拉埃西亚，人们称他为亚努斯·拉弥俄斯，不过忘却会是人尽皆知地爱好诽谤，此名不可全信。”
 “那些人说，雅努斯不只有一张，而是有两张脸孔。对此我要回问：为何只有一张脸？为何只有两张脸？海索与朱利安——据托马斯·洛夫·登曼称——曾经认同‘此诸神兼是亦兼非’雅努斯。但在之后，海索坚称‘兼是’他，科赛利则偏爱单纯的‘兼非’。登曼是个不怀好意的半吊子，但这两种说法听起来各具其实。”

 'Janus is the Gatekeeper, the twin-god, the god that wounds, the presager of changes, the sun, the moon. Description: Or, 'The Refinements of Light'. Julian Coseley had never wanted or expected to write a second edition of his masterwork...
 Julian Coseley long regarded Solomon Husher as a charlatan. But his friend Nina Lagasse painted three paintings before her death in 1895… and these paintings apparently convinced Coseley to change his mind. With considerable irritation, he revised his magnum opus.
 The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. Coseley had always championed History rather than Eternity - the exceptions, limitations, contradictions of freedom. But Husher's and Lagasse's work convinced him to believe in the 'paradox of the eternal ending', a means in which perfection might be reconciled with freedom. He's not happy about it. This is perhaps the angriest book ever written in support of a peaceful philosophy of acceptance. But Coseley was always scrupulous about his conclusions.
output: 名称：《走近基础美学：第二版》 类型：抄本 描述：又名“光之精炼”。朱利安·科赛利从未希望或预料过要给自己的杰作写第二版…… 朱利安·科赛利曾一直认为认为所罗门·赫舍是个江湖骗子。但他的朋友宁娜·拉格斯在1895年去世前留下了三幅画……这些画作显然说服科赛利改变了看法。他相当恼火地修改了自己的杰作。 众司辰的完美霸权或许是永恒的。科赛利总是更愿意捍卫历史而非永恒——自由的例外、限制与矛盾。但是赫舍和拉格斯的研究结果使他不得不转而相信“永恒终结的悖论”，一种能使完美与自由达成和解的途径。他对此并不乐见。在支持平和容忍的哲学书籍中，这可能是有史以来最为愤懑的那本。但是科赛利对自己的结论向来不徇私情。

 “死亡的方向朝下，”书中这样解释，“孔雀之门被认为是一种裂缝，或是一处磨损。但从其他角度看，它更像是一张嘴——或者说是一种更珍贵的入口。”对门扉讨论中包括一种通过这些门召唤生物的仪式，虽然缺失了关键祷词。
output:
Name: A True and Complete Accounting of the Asclepian Mysteries of the Roots of the House
Type: book
Description: Descriptions of the 'Asclepian Mysteries', reproduced by one 'Rylee Grese' from - supposedly - a much older text. It's unlikely to be genuine, but it makes a reference to 'The House without Walls and its Wood', right there in the prologue.
 This is very obviously not an antique text. At the very least, it has been badly mutilated. But it contains substantial intriguing material: especially, a persuasive comparison of the many-portalled House without Walls, to the human body.
 'The direction of Death is down,' the book explains. 'The Peacock Door has been considered a rent, or an abrasion, but in some respects is more like a mouth - if not a more treasured point of entry.' Discussions of the Doors include a rite which may conjure creatures through those doors, although key incantations are missing.

类型：书籍
描述：由靠做雇佣兵，也有时靠家里汇钱过活的帕维尔·舒加在希腊生活时煞费苦心地收集成书。
 身负伤疤的上尉斩杀七怪，平定地面后建立迈锡尼的经过。
 上尉每消灭一怪，血的洪潮就升得更高，直至最后使一名女祭司溺死其中并重生为蛇神。她祝福上尉，上尉则在血潮退却后离开迈锡尼，去向“林地之上的居屋”，成为至高的主宰。
output:
Name: The Deeds of the Scarred Captain
Type: book
Description: Painstakingly assembled by the soldier of fortune and sometime remittance man, Pavel Shulga, during his years in Greece.
 An account of the founding of Mycenae by a 'Scarred Captain' who first slew seven monsters to make the land safe.
 As the Captain destroys each monster, a flood of blood rises higher, until at last a priestess drowns and is reborn as a serpent-goddess. She blesses the Captain, and he departs for the 'House above the Forest', leaving Mycenae to reign supreme after the flood of blood subsides.

input:
Name: Sunset Passages
Type: codex
Description: A miscellany of the funerary prayers, ceremonies and hymns of the Church of the Unconquered Sun, which was ascendant in the Third and Fourth Histories. It schismed during the Intercalate, when the Sun was divided, and has not survived as a significant force.
 The Church revered the Sun-in-Splendour before it was divided - but even while it was still whole, its later selves were recognised as its Names. The Madrugad, of course, presided over death and the passage into the House.
 The White Ceremony was spoken to honour the Madrugad, at funerals held in the chilly space before dawn. The text cautions that all blades should remain sheathed while the Ceremony is spoken, 'lest the corpse be not quiet.'
output:
名称：《日落殊途》
类型：抄本
描述：本书网罗了在第三和第四史中地位显赫的无敌太阳教会——其典礼中的各种祷文，仪式和赞歌。该教派在置闰——即太阳遭到分裂时——发生分裂，留存下来的部分不再具有不可小觑的势力。
 教会在骄阳分裂前就尊崇它——但在骄阳尚完整时，它日后的复数个自我就已经被认为是它的具名者了。而昕旦执掌的自然是死亡和进入居屋的道路。
 “纯白之礼”据称是纪念昕旦的仪式，在拂晓前冷冽之时的葬礼中施行。这份文献提醒道，在念诵仪式祝词时，所有的刀刃都不能出鞘，“否则尸体将不再沉默。”

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, keeping a gothic, symbol-laden style reminiscent of esoteric literature.
input: 瓦伦丁提议说，统治者应当由毒蛇来选举产生，而不是由他们的臣民，“因蛇天性冷血，不可腐蚀。”

instruction: 将下面的英文物品描述翻译为中文，保持类似克苏鲁与哥特式的神秘氛围与仪式感。
input:
Name: The Ascendant
Type: codex
Description: The Edge-long Dardesh boasts of her victories over her brother-enemy Tareg in the days of the Shadowless Empire.
 'Sweeter than wine, than nectar is the blood of my brother. We have raised up armies one against another, we have sated the Blackbone with the sinking of our ships…'
 Dardesh's boasting at length turns melancholy. An Edge-long is half a dyad; she may not defeat her hated brother-enemy without ending herself. She doesn't even want to; but she is aware, to her frustration, that she is 'a piece on the board, an axle on the ox-cart' - an essential part of the eternal engine of contention which the Lionsmith and Colonel use to sustain the world.
output:
名称：《论支配》
类型：抄本
描述：刃之长生者丹德什夸耀了自己在无影帝国时期，与她的“兄敌”塔格的战争中取得的一系列胜利。
 “比酒更甜、比蜜更甜的，是我兄弟的鲜血。我们召集军队彼此攻击。我们击沉对方的船只，使黑骸餍足……”
 丹德什的自夸最终转变为忧郁。一位刃之长生者是对刃的一半；如果不结束自己的生命，她就不可能打败她所讨厌的兄敌。她甚至不想这么做；而令她沮丧的是，她最终意识到自己不过是“棋盘上的棋子，牛车上的车轴”——是狮子匠和上校那永恒纷争引擎用来维系世界的基本组成部分。

input:
Name: The Bee-Keeper's Ends
Type: codex
Description: Dialogues with bees and uses for honey, as erratically recorded by Ricardo Milagro, gardener of Hush House in Musgrave's time.
 Milagro spends an entire chapter on his hatred of wasps, which he describes as 'the Vile Pretenders'.
 Milagro claims that bees retain many traditions passed down from earlier and greater branches of their species, but that they are fiercely jealous of these traditions being passed to lesser insects, and insist above all on an oath of secrecy. Tragically, therefore, he is unable to describe these more substantial and powerful traditions.
output:
名称：《养蜂人的目标》
类型：抄本
描述：一份关于蜜蜂及蜂蜜之妙用的对话体手稿，作者系马斯格雷夫时期噤声居屋的园丁，里卡多·米拉格罗。
 米拉格罗用了整整一章来宣泄他对黄蜂的仇恨，他把黄蜂描述为“卑鄙无耻的冒牌货”。
 米拉格罗声称，蜜蜂保留了许多从其物种更早、更伟大的支系中流传下来的传统，但它们十分忌讳将这些传统传授给次要的昆虫，并以坚守秘密为要。非常不幸的是，他因此无法描述这些更为基本、更加强大的传统。

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《孪蛇密续》
类型：抄本
描述：就在大战打响前夕，“亚历山大·斯派鹭”——基本确定为假名——出版了宣称“蛇身贵族”影响了国际关系的传单。这篇名为《孪蛇密续》的文章是其主要灵感来源。
 描述了兜颈贵胄——一门起源不明的世家望族——如何参与祷告，献祭并作诗祝颂钥匙巨蛇、十字路孪生子和镜子女王。“那迦盘绕，那迦现身于创口，那迦饶过已被伤害者。”
 文献将兜颈贵胄描写为“从其死亡的历史逃入其未死的历史”，声称它们现有一百零八名，然而——作为许多双生异象中的一例——它们在跨出其死亡的史传前，只有五十四名。
output:
Name: The Twin-Serpent Tantra
Type: codex
Description: Just before the outbreak of the Great War, 'Alexander Sparrow' - almost certainly a pseudonym - published leaflets claiming the influence of 'Snake Princes' on world affairs. The text called the Twin-Serpent Tantra was his primary inspiration.
 The Tantra describes the Great Hooded Princes - a dynasty of unclear origin - engaging in prayers, sacrifices and poetry in honour of the Key-Serpent, the Crossroads-Twins and the Mirror-Queen. 'Nagi encircles; Nagi arises from wounds; Nagi spares those who are already harmed.'
 The Great Hooded Princes are described as having 'escaped from the history of their death to a history where they yet live'. The text claims that there are now one hundred and eight of them, but - in one of many instances of twinnedness - before they crossed from their death chronicle, there were only fifty-four.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, preserving the solemn, ritualistic tone and occult atmosphere.
input:
名称：《卡本内克裂教》
类型：抄本
描述：名为忘却会的教团在濒临分裂之际，在一处仅知道名为“卡本内克”的边境建筑内举行了集会，此名典出自传说中渔夫王的城堡。教团内的通晓者与长生者就他们长久以来避免参与的“羽毛与鳞片”之问题进行了辩论。
 其中的一员——也是这场辩论的记录者——描述了他是如何在绝望中于“一卷极度异端的典籍”中找到了某种解决方案，但不敢独自实践。他设法说服了少数同僚与他一同离开卡本内克，而其他人则横渡大海，前往午港。
 在最后的几页中，作者揭露了自己的身份：位列通晓者的学徒安布罗斯·威斯考特，此处他的文风一反常态地严肃。他告诉任何发现本书的人，他已经将自己在前文提到的那本书放回了被他称为“杰弗里院长的隐事”的地方，在那里使用“利米亚典仪”的某些祷文便可再次找回。他希望自己那位“阅读甚多、理解甚多”的继任者能找到一重历史来实现它。
output:
Name: The Carbonek Schism
Type: codex
Description: The order of Obliviates, on the brink of schism, assembles in a Bounds-house identified only as 'Carbonek', after the Fisher-King's castle of legend. There the Know and the Long of the order debate their long policy of non-involvement in 'matters of Feather and Scale'.
 One of their number - the one recording their debates - describes how in desperation he has found some kind of solution in a 'volume of transcendent heresy', but dares not pursue it alone. He convinces a handful of other Obliviates to depart Carbonek with him, while the others cross the sea to Port Noon.
 In the last few pages, the author reveals himself as the Know-adept Ambrose Westcott, writing in an uncharacteristically serious mode. He informs any who should find this work that he has returned the book he spoke of to 'Abbot Geffrey's Secret', where it can be retrieved with certain invocations of the Sacra Limiae. He hopes that one who has read this far, and understood this much, will find a History to determine.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, preserving its restrained but unsettling, myth-tinged tone.
input: “那些人说，雅努斯不只有一张，而是有两张脸孔。对此我要回问：为何只有一张脸？为何只有两张脸？海索与朱利安——据托马斯·洛夫·登曼称——曾经认同‘此诸神兼是亦兼非’雅努斯。但在之后，海索坚称‘兼是’他，科赛利则偏爱单纯的‘兼非’。登曼是个不怀好意的半吊子，但这两种说法听起来各具其实。”
output: 'Janus has, they say, not one face but two. To which I reply: why only one? Why only two? Hersault and Coseley - according to Thomas Love Denman - once agreed that Janus was 'all the gods and none'. But later, Hersault described him as 'all the gods', and Coseley favoured 'none'. Denman was a sinister dilettante, but this rings true of them both.'

Type: book
Description: A volume of collected teachings of the Sisterhood of the Knot, that arcane-contemplative order that existed in all histories, but in some was very powerful indeed. This was recorded by 'Hypatia', and dedicated to St Nympha.
 St Nympha is described as 'not born, but cultivated'. The sentience that became the saint, 'Hypatia' indicates, inhabited a sinner's corpse in order to enable that sinner's redemption.
 'Not all the Dead enter the Mansus by the Winter Door. Not all the Dead enter the Mansus at all.'

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input: 名称：《伊纳姆、卡皮吉吉努皮尔、加尔基、克雷皮斯》 类型：书籍 描述：书中的四个神秘人物讲述了他们多年来在“栖木”——鸟型司辰的集会地——听到的故事。 伊纳姆：拾滩鸦没有分享他的宝藏吗？加尔基：没有分享最稀有的。他把最珍贵的留给自己了，号称那些是他找到的，不是偷来的。 卡皮吉吉努皮尔认为拾滩鸦不仅是盗贼，同时也是探子，甚至喜欢窥淫。他把司辰和祂们的具名者间秘密交合的记忆藏在居屋的角落，作为暗中夸耀的宝藏。还有一个很火的猜测：热情如火的林地司辰环杉，和有时与女巫做姐妹的树中牝马，这两者间有私情。
output:
Name: Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys
Type: book
Description: In which four enigmatic figures tell the stories they've heard over the years at the Roost, the secret location where the aviform Hours congregate.
 INAAM: Has not the Beach-Crow shared his treasures? GARKIE: Not the rarest. He takes those things most precious, which he claims found, not stolen.
 The Beach-Crow, Kapigiginlupir suggests, is not only a thief, but also a spy and even a voyeur. He has hidden the memory of secret couplings among the Hours and their Names in the corners of the House, as treasures to gloat over. There is particularly fevered speculation on a liaison between the Ring-Yew, that fervent Hour of the Wood, and the Mare-in-the-Tree, who sometimes has been the Witch's Sister.

input: Eva Dewulf is engaged to one Abraham Wheelock, but he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again. Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. These include a waxed pouch containing a letter addressed to Wheelock, whose contents seem to show he is a spy in the pay of the Austrians. Subsequent investigations suggest that the letter is a forgery, but the matter remains obscure...
output: 伊娃·德沃尔夫和亚伯拉罕·惠洛克订了婚，他却在婚礼祭坛前毁约，将她抛弃。伊娃在羞耻与愤怒之中回到了布兰库格，再也没有出现在伦敦。她离开三天后，亚伯拉罕·惠洛克的尸体被冲上了格雷夫森德的海岸。他的面部被群鸟啄食得面目全非，只能通过随身物体来辨认——其中包括一封烫有漆印的、寄给惠洛克的信，信的内容似乎表明他是奥地利人雇佣的间谍。后续调查显示信件似乎系伪造，但事件的全貌依然不甚明了……

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, preserving its restrained but unsettling, myth-tinged tone.
input: “马提亚斯爱着成虫。（真的吗？长生者能够恋爱？还是他们的灵魂中的那个器官已干瘪到无法挽回？）成虫爱着马提亚斯。（真的吗？还是她只是一时兴起？）他追寻着她穿过林地，但她在最后绕开了噩梦泥沼，而后他们一起躺在逐渐变亮的边境。于是他们学会了杯之欢愉，这是他们为自己赢得的密传。”
output: 'Matthias loved the Imago. (Did he? Can Long love, or has that organ of their soul desiccated beyond repair?) The Imago loved Matthias. (Did she? or did she only enact a whim?) He pursued her through the Wood, but at the last she turned aside from the nightmare-slough, and they lay together where the Bounds grow bright. Name: Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903
Type: codex
Description: A confidential journal kept by Greene, former Nocturnal Branch Superindent but, by 1903, Librarian of the House. Greene has kept his journal in Hyksos, presumably as an extra measure of privacy.
 In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'
 The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau... 

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.

 “大海从不后悔潮水涨落，”费克里写道，“因为当潮水退去，它会在沙滩上留下痕迹；这痕迹便是大海的记忆。”
 费克里热衷于钓鱼，他在书中也兴致高涨地谈到了布兰库格对鱼的各种烹饪方式。他也承认，对“大海的馈赠”的热忱转变了他——在来到布兰库格之前，他只吃从大地中找到的东西。“故而我过去曾强大得多。但我们每个人都舍弃了曾经的自己，才变成了现在的我们。”

 'The Sea does not regret the tide,' Fekri writes, 'for when the tide has passed, it leaves its traces on the sand; which traces are the Sea's memory.'
 Fekri is a keen fisherman, and speaks glowingly of the fish suppers of Brancrug. He also admits that his enthusiasm for 'the bounty of the sea' has altered him - that before he came to Brancrug, he consumed only those things found in the earth. instruction: Given structured item information, generate a complete English item description.

Type: codex

Learned: Lesson: Pyroglyphics
Based on the information above, write a full English item description in the style of 'Book of Hours', with occult, quasi-religious and symbolic overtones.
output:
Lord Franklin Bancroft was initiated into the arts of the Flowermaker by the 'rose-witch' Fionna Ayrshire. He rose to become a Society provider of occult services and secret pleasures, before his abrupt disappearance in 1790.
 Bancroft seems to have been a talented adept, but devoted his energies to frustratingly whimsical projects: arranging 'grape-fetching races' between Mansus-spirits, teaching Percussigants to juggle, and conjuring storms of imaginary blossoms for the rose-witch Ayrshire, who resolutely refused ever to couple with him. Bancroft spends twenty pages bemoaning this last.
 The Mantra here recorded is a high and exacting magic which can be used to pledge one's spirit to the Watchman, beginning an ascent to the House. Bancroft boasts of his ability to recite it when in his cups. He also had it set to music for a performance with fireworks at Vauxhall Gardens.

output: In the 1800s, Dr Arun Peel was invited to give a series of lectures to the Curia. They combine his pithy view of the Histories with his particular brand of unhelpfully ironical insight. '1776, the Third History: Louis declares the Masque of Masques, and forbids mention of the Great Writhing within the walls of the Palace of Versailles, although by this point the Worms are observed to move openly along the boulevards of Paris, sometimes even in daylight. The Army is redeployed to defend the Court.  作者席描述了人类文明存在之前，“介壳种”所施行的献给最初的司辰——石源诸神的仪式。他称这些信息是最后一名存活的介壳种告诉他的。

input: 名称：De Ratio Quercuum 类型：抄本 描述：标题的拉丁语大意为“橡树之理”；但实际上是纳撒尼尔·达西-埃弗斯对他所能找到的所有树木其神秘学特性的调查，而非仅仅是橡树。本书虽杂乱无章，却引人入胜。 “在波斯，taxus baccata，即紫杉，被称为sorkhdar，意为‘红色的树’。他们对杯之根系早有了解。再后来，本都的伟大国王在最古老的雌树的枝条上安置了蜂箱……” “本都紫杉的浆果开启通往死亡的大门，但它的蜂蜜却能打开一扇截然不同的大门。这不是那位伟大国王的mithridate（万灵药），但饮下了伟大紫杉馈赠的人确实能够百毒不侵。也许他们应该……”但写到这里时，纳撒尼尔被某种墨水的毒性分散了注意力。他确实提到了更加有用的信息，那就是可以使用“根系之仪”，在蜜相的帮助下调制出一种次要的力量之墨，杉瘿墨。
output: Name: De Ratio Quercuum Type: codex Description: In English the title translates roughly as 'the Account of the Oaks'; but this is Nathaniel Darcy-Evers' fascinating, if haphazard, survey of the occult properties of every tree he can find, not just oaks. 'In Persia taxus baccata, the yew, is called sorkhdar, which is 'the red tree'. There they had long understood the Grail-Root. In later times, the Great King of Pontus had bee-hives set in the branches of the oldest of the female trees….' 'The berries of the Pontine Yew open the door to death but the honey of their flowers opens a different door entirely. This was not the Great King's mithridate but one who has suckled at the Great Yew fears poison no longer. Perhaps they should…' Nathaniel is here distracted, however, by the toxic properties of certain inks. He does mention more usefully that the minor Ink of Power, Yewgall, can be brewed through the Rites of the Roots with the assistance of the aspect Nectar.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese item description into English, keeping a sombre, quasi-religious and slightly Lovecraftian style.
input:
名称：《琥珀之光》
类型：抄本
描述：“炽焰”奥马尔为了清偿自己熄灭圣焰的罪过，在推罗看了七年灯塔。而在这场苦役最后，他对火焰产生了莫大的恐惧，甚至无法与烛焰共处一室。写这本书是他苦修的一部分。
 奥马尔声称名为守夜人的司辰既是肉源神——原为凡人的司辰——也是光源神——降自辉光的司辰——但在最后又补充说，守夜人有三重来源，即是说“实质上，他是琥珀神”。
 守夜人，据奥马尔称，原先完全是另外一位司辰，因其他司辰欲将其赶进虚界而逃入辉光，升入其间。奥马尔讲到这点时可能渗入了他自己的偏见：可想而知，此处的行文变得不那么连贯。书的最后一部分致力于证明眼瞳，卵和太阳在某种意义上是一体的。
output:
Name: The Focus of Amber
Type: codex
Description: Omar, the Blaze, spent seven years manning a lighthouse in Tyre, in atonement for the extinguishing of a sacred flame. By the end of his stint, he was so terrified of fire that he could not stand to share a room with a candle. This work was written in partial penance.
 Omar claims that the Hour called Watchman is both a god-who-was-flesh - an Hour who was mortal - and also a god-from-Light - an Hour who descended from the Glory - but adds, finally, that the Watchman's origin is triple, and that 'in essence, he is Amber.'
 The Watchman, according to Omar, was once another Hour entirely, who ascended into the Glory to escape efforts by other Hours to send him to Nowhere. It may be that Omar's sense of persecution creeps into the narrative at this point: certainly it grows less coherent, and the last part is devoted to attempts to prove that eyes, eggs and the Sun are all in some sense conjunct.

 拉孔布坚称，那些物品都得到了妥善的利用；他还嘲笑夜勤处是“根冠的走狗”。令人不安的是，在审讯的最后几分钟，他开始坚持审讯者应该“烧掉图书馆”。他对自己想看到的那股火焰充满狂热，这导致了一阵剧烈的咳嗽，审讯在此戛然而止。

Name: Velletri Interviews
Type: record
Description: Interrogation of a man named Lacombe, a former Nocturnal Branch inspector now identified as 'terminally robigoid'.
 Lacombe is not especially lucid, and the state called 'robigoia' evidently includes a malady of the lungs which causes coughing fits: he weakens audibly over the course of the interrogation. He is questioned about the disposition of various unsanctioned items recovered from a Nocturnal Branch raid on a castle at Ortucchio, in the region of the Fucine Marshes. He is, however, defiant as well as incoherent.
 Lacombe insists the items have been put to good use; he derides Nocturnal Branch as 'the lackeys of Calyptra'. Alarmingly, during the last few minutes of the interrogation, he begins to insist that his interrogator should 'burn the Library'. He waxes enthusiastic about the fire he wants to see, leading to a final coughing fit after which the interview abruptly ends.

In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'

欧内斯汀·彼得汉斯记录了她对岛上树木与花卉生长状况的观察结果，以及她尝试从中汲取的预示与征兆——尤其是布莱恩伯爵甸的那棵紫杉，它有时会开出反常的花朵。

The diaries of the explorer and murderer Lars Westergren. He's unhelpfully translated them into Phrygian, for privacy.
 'There are map-legends, there are maps of legends, and there are legends of maps. Aspects of the Mansus subsist in all of these, in much the same way that you find water in a swamp and in a cup and in the sky.'

Name: The High Traditions of the Noble Endeavour
Type: codex
Description: A blandly positive work on the Endeavour Club, published by the Endeavour Club. The Club was founded in 1862 but claims to draw from much older traditions.
 Club members are assigned names out of noble myth - 'Jaufre', 'Roland', and, unexpectedly, 'Breadbeddel'. They claim to be heirs to the Leashed Flame, which gave the island of Britain such appalling power in some histories.
 Their 'Endeavour' itself is a purifying fire which makes its fuel something more than human. This transformation, however, is no longer encouraged by the Club, and perhaps - the work is coy on this - no longer permitted.

Description: Battle-apothegms of the Name Quirinus.

 When Quirinus was honoured in Rome, he was sometimes associated with the enigmatic god Janus - especially in the rites of the Unnumbered Legion. The advice in these pages doesn't confirm any such connection, but does suggest a more philosophical side to this warrior-Name.

 “居屋的法则禁止马提亚斯去爱，而林地的习俗也禁止那只成虫停留。所以在她亮出阿拉卡城的剪刀时，他最后一次将她唤来；她使他忍痛减去她背后的翅膀，这样她就能留下；而他使她忍痛剪去他存放男性种籽的部位，这样他们就能远离‘罪恶行径’。这便是满含血与欢乐的爱情。我们已将马提亚斯逐出居屋。”
 “在树根的摇篮之中，马提亚斯和成虫留下了他们的名字，虽然他们的名字早已失却，但他们找到了自己的‘命名日之谜’。我们可以用‘溶解与离析’重新唤起那谜团，从而在飞蛾的见证下，将我们的记忆变成我们的未来。请明智地使用这个技艺，不要忘记那对为了能一起被遗忘而舍弃自己过去的具名者和长生者。”

Type: codex

 'The laws of the House forbade Matthias to love. The customs of the Wood forbade the Imago to remain. So he conjured her a final time, when she had uncovered the Shears of Alakapura; and she suffered him to cut the wings from her back, so that she might remain; and he suffered her to cut the parts which hold man's seed, to keep them from the Detestable Act. This was love in all its blood and joy. We have cast out Matthias from the House.'
 'In the cradle of the roots, Matthias and the Imago left their names, and though their names were lost, they found their Nameday Riddles. This we recall in Solution and Separation, so that in the presence of the Moth our memories may become our futures. Do this wisely, in memory of the Name and the Long who gave up their past that they might be together forgotten.'

 教会在骄阳分裂前就尊崇它——但在骄阳尚完整时，它日后的复数个自我就已经被认为是它的具名者了。而昕旦执掌的自然是死亡和进入居屋的道路。

 The Church revered the Sun-in-Splendour before it was divided -but even while it was still whole, its later selves were recognised as its Names. The Madrugad, of course, presided over death and the passage into the House.

instruction: Translate the following Chinese passage into English, keeping the same sense of mystery, philosophical depth and occult symbolism.
input: 宁娜伽勒称：在石源神进入漫宿的时代，孔雀之门并不存在。祂们用“獠牙之钥”开启了凡人通常无法开启的狂暴之门。“正如喀俄涅的门徒所言，言辞即是伤口。令我担忧的是，经此伤口，漫宿的血流淌至今，终有一日，言辞将终结梦境。我担心此事；但我更担心另一种情况。”
output: The Peacock Door did not exist - Ninegala says - in the days when the gods-from-stone entered the Mansus. They used the 'Fanged Key' to open the Savage Door, a door not usually available to mortals. 'Speech, as the initiates of Chione would have it, is a wound. output: 'The Law goes back all the way to Stone: the Keys cannot be held or owned. This had, I believe, the unexpected consequence that those outside the law may hold and own them. But even they cannot keep them. And of course a Key is no more physical than a spirit. But a spirit may be housed in a body, and I have touched a Key with my own hands.'
